# ColumnStructure — how the two columns multiply

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean

A product of two numbers from the 6n-1 column lands in the 6n+1 column, and so on for all four combinations; each prime above 3 hits the 6n-1 column at exactly one position per cycle; every number in the 6n-1 column has a prime factor from that same column.

## Claims

<a id="columns_multiply"></a>
### `columns_multiply`

How the 6n-1 and 6n+1 columns multiply into each other.

```lean
/-- **How the columns multiply.** (6n-1)·(6n-1) lands in 6n+1; (6n-1)·(6n+1)
and (6n+1)·(6n-1) land in 6n-1; (6n+1)·(6n+1) lands in 6n+1. -/
def columns_multiply : Prop :=
  ∀ a b : Nat,
    (∃ n, col_minus a * col_minus b = col_plus n) ∧
    (∃ n, col_minus a * col_plus b = col_minus n) ∧
    (∃ n, col_plus a * col_minus b = col_minus n) ∧
    (∃ n, col_plus a * col_plus b = col_plus n)
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ColumnStructure.columns_multiply_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean)

<a id="col_minus_periodicity"></a>
### `col_minus_periodicity`

Each prime other than 2 and 3 divides the 6n-1 column at exactly one position per cycle.

```lean
/-- **Each prime hits the 6n-1 column once per cycle.** For a prime other than
2 and 3 there is exactly one position, below the prime, at which it divides
the 6n-1 column: it divides the entry at a position exactly when that
position leaves this remainder on division by the prime. -/
def col_minus_periodicity : Prop :=
  ∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → p ≠ 2 → p ≠ 3 →
    ∃ n_p : Nat, n_p < p ∧ ∀ n : Nat, p ∣ col_minus n ↔ n % p = n_p
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.ColumnStructure.col_minus_periodicity_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean)

<a id="col_minus_has_minus_prime_factor"></a>
### `col_minus_has_minus_prime_factor`

Every 6n-1 number has a 6n-1 prime factor.

```lean
/-- **Every 6n-1 number has a 6n-1 prime factor.** -/
def col_minus_has_minus_prime_factor : Prop :=
  ∀ n : Nat, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ col_minus n ∧ p % 6 = 5
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.ColumnStructure.col_minus_has_minus_prime_factor_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)

<a id="col_minus_composite_has_proper_minus_factor"></a>
### `col_minus_composite_has_proper_minus_factor`

A composite 6n-1 number has a smaller 6n-1 prime factor.

```lean
/-- **A composite 6n-1 number has a smaller 6n-1 prime factor.** -/
def col_minus_composite_has_proper_minus_factor : Prop :=
  ∀ n : Nat, ¬ (col_minus n).Prime →
    ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ∣ col_minus n ∧ p % 6 = 5 ∧ p < col_minus n
```

**Rests on:** [`Wheel6.prime_gt_three_is_candidate`](Wheel6.md#prime_gt_three_is_candidate)

**Proof:** `RNS.ColumnStructure.col_minus_composite_has_proper_minus_factor_step` in [`RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/ColumnStructure.lean); joined to its inputs in [`RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/Assemble.lean)
